IonQ vs. Rigetti: Is the Quantum Rally Backed by Fundamentals, or Just Momentum?
Sat, October 3, 2026 at 7:34 AM PDT 5 min read
IonQ, Inc. (NYSE:IONQ) jumped roughly 12% in premarket trading on September 23 after testing the industry's first real-time quantum error decoder, then extended gains on reveals that its Superion quantum processor would be integrated into NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center with Rigetti Computing, Inc. (NASDAQ:RGTI) trading up in sympathy on the same announcement, as the two stocks typically move together on sector-validating news. That said, a shared rally obscures a valuation gap between the two that's far wider than most sector-wide coverage lets on.
Curious to see how far Wall Street thinks the rally will go? BofA recently put a $60 price target on IonQ, here's the bull case in full.
IonQ's second-quarter revenue came in at $80 million, up 287% year-over-year, and management boosted its 2026 projection to $280-290 million, with combined revenue (after closing the SkyWater foundry purchase) potentially reaching $460 million for the year. The company had roughly $2 billion in pro-forma cash, cash equivalents and investments following the SkyWater acquisition, dwarfing Rigetti's approximately $540 million, giving IonQ significantly more runway to fund years of pre-commercial R&D without fear of dilution.
On the tech front, IonQ's trapped-ion design appears to have an accuracy advantage in recent comparisons, with IonQ reporting strong two-qubit gate-fidelity results, although direct comparisons with Rigetti are not straightforward. However, Rigetti's architecture offers an advantage in terms of speed. The distinction is significant because quantum computing is not a simple race in which one company is "ahead" on every metric: accuracy, gate speed, scalability, connectivity, and error correction are all important. IonQ's advantage is thus best regarded as a technical and financial one, rather than proof that it has already won the architecture race. Rigetti remains open to the potential that advancements in speed, production, or error correction could close the gap.
The valuation gap gets flattened when these two stocks are discussed together. IonQ's market capitalization is currently around $17.48 billion, compared to combined 2026 revenue guidance of $450 million to $460 million following the SkyWater acquisition, putting its forward price-to-sales multiple in the 39x range. This is already a notable multiple, but it is built on a path to nearly triple-digit revenue growth and a roughly $2 billion of pro-forma cash, cash equivalents and investments that reduces near-term funding risk.
Meanwhile, Rigetti, with a market capitalization that has fluctuated between $5 billion to $9 billion over the last year, trades at an unusual trailing price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 391.65x, having previously reached nearly 1,000x during substantial trading spikes.
While trailing multiples for both businesses remain elevated due to small historical sales bases, the valuation gap remains substantial. Simply put, the market is charging investors much more per dollar of current revenue for Rigetti than for IonQ, despite IonQ having a far stronger balance sheet and a larger revenue base.
That disparity becomes significant because it signals potential downside risk if sentiment cools. A stock trading at 39x forward sales has priced in high growth, while a stock trading at several hundred times trailing sales has priced in near-perfect execution over a much longer time horizon, with far less revenue currently on the books to anchor that multiple if the growth narrative stalls even briefly.
Insider selling adds another cautious signal to the group. Since September 2024, insiders at IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave, and Quantum Computing Inc. have collectively sold around $895.1 million more stock than they bought. On September 11, IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi sold 16,121 shares for around $598,000, though the filing said that the transaction was non-discretionary and was used to meet tax obligations related to vested restricted stock units.
Hedge fund positioning has grown for both companies, although Rigetti Computing, Inc. (NASDAQ:RGTI) has seen a greater gain. The number of hedge funds owning IonQ, Inc. (NYSE:IONQ) jumped from 39 in the first quarter to 42 in the second, while Rigetti's ownership increased from 29 to 34 funds. That suggests that institutional investors are increasing exposure to the quantum theme rather than focusing solely on the better-capitalized leader. The short-interest numbers reflect a far wider contrast over Rigetti: short interest is 10.15% of IonQ's shares versus 19.07% for Rigetti.
Neither stock is a value investment, since both remain speculative bets on a technology that is still years away from widespread commercial application. However, the valuation math argues for treating them very differently within that assumption. IonQ's multiple, while extreme by any conventional measure, is supported by a larger revenue base, faster reported growth, and a cash position that provides years of runway without dilution risk. Rigetti's multiple requires investors to pay several times more per dollar of current sales for a company with a fraction of the cash cushion, implying that any slowdown in its growth rate or the need to raise capital would cause the stock to fall from a far less defensible valuation baseline. Investors drawn to the sector by names like these should treat the price-to-sales gap, not just the shared NVIDIA headline, as the more important number, and should keep an eye on upcoming quarters to see if Rigetti's own revenue growth can actually close that multiple gap, or if the current premium is simply compensation that the market hasn't yet demanded fully.

Those deals sit alongside IonQ's integration into top-tier research efforts. During benchmark runs, the system simulated up to 408 logical qubits and handled more than 31.5 million quantum operations. The demonstration matters because reliable error correction is widely viewed as a prerequisite for practical quantum computing, and the ability to manage such complex calculations without specialized chips lays groundwork for future architectures.
Separately, the company's development team has validated models for change detection in high-resolution satellite radar data on its own hardware — another sign that IonQ's ion-trap architecture is finding commercial traction beyond the lab.
On the administrative side, the New York Stock Exchange filed documents with the SEC to formally delist and deregister IonQ's redeemable warrants. The move is a housekeeping step that simplifies the company's capital structure.

Partnerships spanning industry and academia demonstrate real demand for the company's technology. The road to those 2027 deployments will remain volatile — that comes with the territory for a key technology of this magnitude — but for those with the patience to see it through, the current valuation offers an interesting starting position.

IonQ Announces Increased Full-Year 2026 Financial Outlook Following SkyWater Acquisition
COLLEGE PARK, Md. – Sept. 8, 2026 – IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), the world’s leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry, today announced that, for the full year 2026, it expects revenue to be between $450 million and $460 million. This outlook includes the contributions of SkyWater Technology beginning on July 31, 2026, the date it was acquired by IonQ, through to Dec. 31, 2026. It also reflects elimination of estimated intercompany revenues under the pre-existing commercial agreement between IonQ and Skywater.
“As we prepare to host our first joint Investor Day today, our updated full-year guidance highlights both the market traction of our quantum platform and the foundational manufacturing scale provided by SkyWater,” said Niccolo de Masi, Chairman & CEO of IonQ. De Masi continued, “We are now executing on a shared roadmap that accelerates our timeline and capabilities to achieve commercial-scale, fault tolerant quantum computing."
“Releasing our first combined guidance as a unified organization is a pivotal step that demonstrates the immediate financial and operational strength of bringing IonQ and SkyWater together,” said Inder Singh, CFO & COO of IonQ.
IonQ will host a webcast at 12:30 PM Eastern time today. The call will be available live via webcast on the Company’s website here, or directly here. An archive of the webcast will be available here shortly after the call and will remain available for one year.
IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and foundry - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems. Earlier systems have helped customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, AstraZeneca, and NVIDIA achieve a 20x performance increase over previous quantum solutions and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.
Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations across North America, Latin America, EMEA, and APAC. Our quantum computing services have been available through all major cloud providers since 2021, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing
customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. Learn more at IonQ.com.

IonQ Appoints Dr. Eric Ball and Timothy Baxter to Board of Directors
Board Additions Support Next Phases of IonQ Growth
COLLEGE PARK, Md. — Aug. 25, 2026 — IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), the world’s leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry, today announced the appointment of two new board members: technology finance expert Dr. Eric Ball, and former SkyWater Technology Chairman and Samsung North America CEO Timothy Baxter. Each brings accretive experience to support IonQ’s next phases of expansion.
“We’re making the leap to rapid scalability in quantum computing manufacturing, in parallel with integrating all components of our unique quantum platform,” said IonQ Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi. “Our responsibilities as the leading quantum merchant supplier are significant, as are the advances we expect to make in quantum computing due to our pioneering vertical integration. Eric and Tim bring complementary insights and firsthand expertise to our Board and leadership team.”
Dr. Ball has nearly 40 years in senior financial roles at public companies, among them AT&T, Cisco, and Flextronics, including 10 years as Senior Vice President and Treasurer at Oracle. There, he arranged $52 billion of financing and served on the M&A teams for over 100 acquisitions. The author of two books, with a PhD in Management Economics, Dr. Ball has also taught economics at three universities and is a member of multiple corporate and non-profit boards.
Timothy Baxter was Chairman of the SkyWater Technology Board of Directors until the company’s recently completed acquisition by IonQ. With over 40 years of experience leading major technology companies, including senior management roles at AT&T, Sony, and Samsung, where he rose to CEO of Samsung, North America. He helped launch numerous next generation technologies including 5G, HDTV and Blu-ray and currently serves on several private and publicly traded boards.
